controlFields.Anti-dependency: Architectural approach that structurally prevents users from forming attachment to the tool
controlFields.Cooldown period: Enforced waiting period between sessions to prevent compulsive usage
controlFields.Action commitment gate: Interface element requiring users to commit to real-world actions before continuing tool use
controlFields.Limerence: Involuntary state of intense romantic attachment characterised by intrusive thinking, emotional dependency, and compulsive rituals
controlFields.Limerence transfer: Formation of limerent attachment to the tool itself, replacing the original limerent object
controlFields.Ritual tracking: Monitoring of limerent behaviours (social media checking, route-taking, mental rehearsal) over time
controlFields.Phase assessment: Evaluation of which limerence phase a user is in (infatuation, crystallisation, deterioration, resolution)
controlFields.Special category data: UK GDPR classification for sensitive data including health data, requiring Article 9 lawful basis
controlFields.Zero-retention: Contractual guarantee that a data processor does not store user content beyond the processing transaction
controlFields.Warmth detection: Safety filter that identifies AI responses simulating emotional warmth or connection
controlFields.Recovery velocity: Rate at which users reduce limerent symptoms and disengage from the tool
controlFields.UK GDPR: Data protection framework governing all personal data processing, with Article 9 for special category health data
controlFields.UK GDPR Article 9: Lawful basis required for processing special category (health) data
controlFields.UK GDPR Article 25: Privacy by design and by default
controlFields.UK GDPR Article 35: Data Protection Impact Assessment requirement for high-risk processing

controlFields.Collection minimisation: Only data necessary for the stated purposes is collected. No browsing data, device telemetry, location data, or social media data. Email is hashed at point of collection -- raw email is never stored (DR-001).
controlFields.Processing minimisation: LLM receives pseudonymised user_id only (INT-001). No PII is included in LLM prompts. Ritual names are stored but not analysed by AI -- they serve as user-facing labels only.
controlFields.Retention minimisation: Session data auto-deleted after 12 months. Account data deleted within 30 days of deletion request. Raw ritual data follows session retention. Only summary/trend data retained long-term.
controlFields.Access minimisation: Row Level Security enforces per-user data isolation at database level (ADR-006). No admin access to decrypted session content without explicit justification.
controlFields.Risk Description: Users creating multiple accounts to bypass cooldown periods (8-hour minimum between sessions) create duplicate user profiles with fragmented data. This undermines data accuracy, complicates subject access requests, and defeats anti-dependency constraints designed to protect the user from excessive tool use.
controlFields.Data Categories Affected: DR-001 (duplicate profiles), DR-002 (fragmented session history), DR-003 (incomplete ritual tracking)
controlFields.Harm to Individuals: Fragmented data means ritual tracking and phase assessment are based on incomplete information, reducing clinical effectiveness. User exercising data subject rights (SAR, erasure) may not realise they have data across multiple accounts. The circumvention itself indicates the user may be forming dependency on the tool -- the anti-dependency constraint exists to protect them.
controlFields.Mitigations: Multi-account prevention using privacy-proportionate device fingerprinting (FR-013, ADR-005); email uniqueness check at registration (email_hash uniqueness constraint in DR-001); detection heuristics for account creation patterns; user education during onboarding about why cooldowns exist (protecting recovery, not restricting access); account linking capability if duplicate detected (with user consent)
controlFields.Zero-retention DPA: Data Processing Agreement under which the processor commits to not storing any data at rest
controlFields.Age gating: Users must confirm they are 18+ during account creation (DR-001, age_confirmed boolean)
controlFields.No child-specific content: Tool is designed for adult users. No age-appropriate content for under-18s exists.
controlFields.Scope exclusion: Support for minors is explicitly out of scope and would require a separate safeguarding framework, parental consent architecture, and Age Appropriate Design Code compliance
controlFields.Training data: DeLimerence does not fine-tune the LLM on user data. No user conversations contribute to model training.
controlFields.Model bias: LLM may have biases in understanding limerence (undertrained on this rare condition) or cultural biases in relationship norms
controlFields.Hallucination: LLM may generate clinically inaccurate psychoeducation or inappropriate intervention advice
controlFields.Prompt injection: Adversarial users may attempt to bypass anti-dependency constraints or extract system prompt
controlFields.Explainability: Users should understand why the AI responds as it does

controlFields.Phase assessment: Classification of user's current limerence stage: initiation, crystallisation, deterioration, or resolution
controlFields.Ritual: Compulsive behaviour associated with limerence (e.g., checking social media, rereading messages, engineering encounters)

controlFields.Intermittent reinforcement: Variable reward schedule (like a slot machine) that prevents habituation and maximises dopamine response

controlFields.ERP: Exposure and Response Prevention — CBT technique adapted from OCD treatment; involves resisting compulsive rituals
controlFields.ABCDE framework: Cognitive restructuring model: Activating event, Belief, Consequences, Disputation, Effective new approach

controlFields.Distribution: Project team, Clinical Advisory Board, Ethics Review Panel
Project team, Clinical Advisory Board, Ethics Review Panel, potential funders
controlFields.UK Online Safety Act: Counters AI-enabled harms; positions limerence as a recognised exploitation vector for sextortion and CSEA
controlFields.MHRA/NICE Digital Health Innovation: Contributes to digital mental health intervention evidence base; engages with MHRA AI Airlock regulatory sandbox
controlFields.AISI Mission: Demonstrates practical systemic AI safety through anti-dependency architecture; addresses AI companion app risks
controlFields.AI Assurance: Anti-dependency architecture, clinical safety layer, and session constraints serve as a reference implementation of responsible AI design in a high-stakes domain
controlFields.Benefits delivered: 100% -- full clinical evidence base, regulatory certainty, international credibility, all spending objectives met
controlFields.Risk: NIHR/Wellcome grant cycles are 12-18 months. Delays beta launch significantly beyond Q4 2026 target. Over-engineered for current evidence base (one case study). Academic lead requirement may reduce founder control.
controlFields.Feasibility: Achievable but slow. Grant timelines incompatible with SO-1 (Q4 2026 beta).
controlFields.Assessment: **Highest impact but slowest** -- appropriate for Phase 2 after beta validation demonstrates outcomes. Premature at current evidence maturity.
controlFields.Direct competitors: None. No product exists in the anti-dependency AI space for limerence.
controlFields.Adjacent competitors: Woebot, Wysa, Replika (companion). All are engagement-maximising. Structurally unable to pivot to anti-dependency without undermining their business models.
controlFields.Market readiness: Pre-market. Limerence is not a recognised clinical diagnosis (no ICD/DSM code). Market creation required through evidence generation and awareness.
controlFields.Competitive moat: Anti-dependency architecture is structurally incompatible with engagement-maximising business models. Competitors would need to accept declining user engagement as a success metric.
controlFields.Year 1 funding required: GBP 108,514 -- within range of AISI seed grant (GBP 200,000) alone
controlFields.Founder self-funding requirement: GBP 0-40,000 for bridge funding between grant applications and disbursement
controlFields.Revenue dependency: None. Project is fundable as a public good / research project without revenue. Revenue model (if developed) provides upside only.

controlFields.Anti-dependency architecture: System design that structurally prevents users from forming psychological attachment to the tool, inverting standard engagement-maximising patterns
